clue.text: Floor reflecting groundwork by law

indicators.note: reflecting, as in a mirror, turns the word for groundwork back to front

parts.note: prep is preparatory work, the groundwork done beforehand
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A lawyer's notes about laying a floor, mirrored and legalistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor' looks like a noun but is the verb: to floor someone is to baffle them.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone, in the informal sense, is to baffle or confound them completely.

clue.text: Touring circuits, clock up passes

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece wraps around the other
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: to clock is slang for to see or notice
laps are circuits of a track

explanation.surface: A runner on circuits watching the clock as time goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' looks like a timepiece but is the slang verb to notice; 'up' turns it round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that passes is time that goes by, a straightforward synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Sauce of patriot finally investing in foreign currency

indicators.note: investing in means putting money, here a letter, inside something

parts.note: the peso is the currency of Mexico and other countries

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of patriot

explanation.surface: A patriot finally putting money into foreign currency, with sauce thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes T from patriot; 'investing in' puts it inside PESO.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil-and-pine-nut paste from Genoa is a classic Italian pasta sauce.

clue.text: Boffin Bill after something composed of yellow and white, gas

indicators.note: after places the word for bill behind the other two pieces in a down clue

parts.words: something composed of yellow and white
parts.note: an egg is made of a yellow yolk and the white
He is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up

explanation.surface: A scientist named Bill fiddling with yolks and gas in a lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is a poster; 'after' places it last.
explanation.definitionFit: A boffin is British slang for a brainy scientist or intellectual, the same as a highbrow.

clue.text: Pain cutting ear, then doctor back

indicators.note: cutting here means trimming the word for ear short by its last letter

parts.note: lug is slang for an ear
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
back, as in 'years back', means ago

explanation.surface: A patient with earache who then sees a doctor about their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a body part to go with the pain, but it means AGO. 'cutting' trims LUG to LU.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a specific pain: an ache in the muscles of the lower spine.

clue.text: Say, 1, 3 or 5 score units, as a discipline

parts.note: 1, 3 and 5 are examples of odd numbers, i.e. not even; 'Say' marks them as examples
a musical score is divided into measures, its basic units

explanation.surface: Scoring a competition with odd marks, as a matter of discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: One of several gymnastics apparatus answers in this puzzle; 'score' is music, not a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Asymmetric bars set at different heights are a women's gymnastics apparatus and event.

clue.text: Music maker beginning to bark in the style of a dog who was out of this world

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of bark

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of

parts.words: a dog who was out of this world
parts.note: Laika was the Soviet dog sent into orbit in 1957

explanation.surface: An instrument barking like the famous space dog.
explanation.definitionFit: This triangular Russian string instrument is something that makes music.

clue.text: Nag about nines when one over the eight, stimulating stuff

indicators.note: about means going around, so the horse word wraps the shuffled letters

parts.note: a gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse, as is nag

indicators.note: one over the eight is British slang for drunk, so the letters of nines reel about

explanation.surface: A drunk punter nagging about nines and the eight, needing a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when one over the eight' is British slang for tipsy, making the anagram; the shuffled letters are INSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The root is taken as a tonic supposed to boost energy, so it is a stimulant.

clue.text: Discipline, with ban on lying?

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the second piece below the first

parts.note: lying means flat, level rather than upright
to bar something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A disciplinary rule banning lying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' suggests untruths but means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: The high bar is a men's gymnastics apparatus and the event performed on it.

clue.text: See 23 and 6
Servile pair of lackeys starting to open vessel, accessing the ship's drink

indicators.note: accessing means getting into, so the inner pieces go inside the drink

parts.note: grog is rum and water, the traditional sailors' drink

indicators.note: to open means cutting into, so the pair goes inside the vessel word

parts.note: a vein is a blood vessel

indicators.note: pair of asks for the letter twice
starting picks the first letter of lackeys

explanation.surface: Two servants opening a barrel to get at the ship's rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a blood vessel. Two Ls from 'starting' go into VEIN, and that into GROG.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abjectly obsequious, fawning on a superior, is a servile manner.

clue.text: A pommel horse on terra firma

indicators.note: to pommel, a variant of pummel, is to beat, so these letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A gymnast on the pommel horse, feet planted on solid ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pommel horse' looks like the gymnastics apparatus; 'pommel' is the verb pummel, rearranging HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land rather than at sea is to be on solid ground.

clue.text: Masses drifting away, slice of cake ultimately getting wasted

indicators.note: getting wasted means getting drunk, so these letters stagger into a new order
ultimately picks the last letter of cake

explanation.surface: Someone getting drunk while a slice of cake drifts off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting wasted' rearranges SLICE OF plus E from 'ultimately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating slabs of frozen sea are masses that drift away on the current.

clue.text: In store, get beyond Italy to explore by boat

indicators.note: beyond means coming after the letter for Italy

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: In places the word for get inside the word for store

parts.note: a shop is a store
to land something is to get it, as in landing a job

explanation.surface: Shopping in Italy, then heading off to explore by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is the verb as in landing a job, not part of 'get beyond'.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel from one island to the next is a way of exploring an archipelago, usually by boat.

clue.text: Capital distanced from affairs in unions

indicators.note: the capital, i.e. the initial letter, of the word for affairs is removed from it

parts.note: dalliances are flirtations or casual affairs

explanation.surface: A capital city's politicians keeping their distance from affairs within unions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city; it is the first letter, D, dropped from DALLIANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacts and coalitions between parties or nations are formal unions.

clue.text: See 17
Discipline suffering in part of the orchestra

indicators.note: in puts the word for suffering inside the orchestra section

parts.note: the violins, violas, cellos and basses form a section of the orchestra
ill means unwell, suffering

explanation.surface: A player suffering in the violin section, under strict discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging gymnastic hoops held motionless are a men's apparatus and event.

clue.text: Labour Party clipped in the end

indicators.note: in places the shortened party word inside the word for end

parts.note: the tail is the end of something

indicators.note: clipped means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a rave is a big dance party

explanation.surface: The Labour Party getting cut back in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour Party' reads as the political party; 'Labour' is the definition and 'Party' gives RAVE, clipped to RAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Painful toil, or the effort of childbirth, is hard labour.

clue.text: Wave going over as two loose packs in the hold

indicators.note: going over means covering, so the wave word wraps the other letters

parts.note: to sway is to wave from side to side

indicators.note: loose means free or unfixed, so these letters move about

explanation.surface: A wave sweeping over the ship as cargo comes loose in the hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' makes TOWSA from the anagram; 'packs' is a verb, someone packing themselves away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hides aboard a ship has packed themselves secretly into the hold.

clue.text: Close to Moscow I note, a US city

indicators.note: close to picks the last letter of Moscow

parts.note: a chit is a short note

explanation.surface: Someone near Moscow writing a note about an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest city in Kansas, in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Germany and Thailand have abandoned a theatrical old language

indicators.note: have abandoned means the two countries' letters are taken out

parts.note: dramatic means theatrical
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: Two countries walking out of a melodramatic production.
explanation.walkthrough: D and T come out of A DRAMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: This Semitic tongue was spoken in the ancient Near East and in Jesus's time.

clue.text: Margin required to fit in male shoe

indicators.note: to fit in means the margin word goes inside the male word

parts.note: a son is a male child
a lip is an edge or margin

explanation.surface: Leaving room in a man's shoe for a good fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer-style shoe without laces is one you put on without fastening.

clue.text: Discipline shown by the whole island cutting fish

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the other pieces go inside the fish word

parts.note: parr are young salmon
all means the whole
Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: An island's entire population cutting up fish with discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: Parr are young salmon, a fish name crosswords favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Twin rails at equal height are a men's gymnastics apparatus and event.

clue.text: Wheels about 45 inches once, in vault

indicators.note: about means going round, so the wheels word surrounds the measure

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
the ell was an old English cloth measure of 45 inches

explanation.surface: Measuring a car's wheels in an underground vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' might suggest gymnastics, as in the theme, but here it is an underground room.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground storeroom, especially one for wine, is a vault.

clue.text: Destination getting into Tripoli by air?

indicators.note: getting into means the word sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A traveller's destination: flying into Tripoli.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripoli is the capital of the country hidden, so the surface points straight at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African country is a place where a flight ends up, a destination.

clue.text: Box for an emperor, Giza by the sound of it — more than one of those?

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the words are to be said aloud

parts.note: a czar's coffer, a box for an emperor, followed by Giza, the Egyptian pyramid site, said quickly

explanation.surface: An emperor's coffin at Giza, asking whether there might be several.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose sound-alike: 'czar coffer' gives the start and Giza's opening gives the end. 'those' points back to the boxes for an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone coffins for pharaohs are plural here, many such boxes rather than a single one.

clue.text: See 29
Winding up, caught behind

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a team behind in a match is trailing, failing to win

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator on a batter caught behind the stumps, wrapping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught behind' is a cricket dismissal (caught by the wicketkeeper), but here it splits into C and LOSING.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing something to an end is a sense of finishing off, as in a final speech.

clue.text: Discipline required to put scales on ray

parts.note: scales are a weighing instrument with two pans
a ray of light is also called a shaft

explanation.surface: Discipline needed to put scales on a fish, the ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' and 'ray' suggest a fish; they are a weighing device and a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrow raised plank is a women's gymnastics apparatus and event.
